section.heading: Use the Definition of Percent
section.paragraph: How many cents are in one dollar? There are $$100$$ cents in a dollar. How many years are in a century? There are $$100$$ years in a century. Does this give you a clue about what the word “percent” means? It is really two words, “per cent,” and means per one hundred. A percent is a ratio whose denominator is $$100.$$ We use the percent symbol $$\text{\%,}$$ to show percent.

note.title: Percent
note.paragraph: A percent is a ratio whose denominator is $$100.$$

section.paragraph: According to data from the American Association of Community Colleges $$(2015),$$ about $$\text{57\%}$$ of community college students are female. This means $$57$$ out of every $$100$$ community college students are female, as Figure 6.2 shows. Out of the $$100$$ squares on the grid, $$57$$ are shaded, which we write as the ratio $$\frac{57}{100}.$$

image.alt: The figure shows a hundred flat with 57 units shaded.

figure.caption: Among every $$100$$ community college students, $$57$$ are female.

section.paragraph: Similarly, $$\text{25\%}$$ means a ratio of $${\frac{25}{100},} \text{3\%}$$ means a ratio of $$\frac{3}{100}$$ and $$\text{100\%}$$ means a ratio of $$\frac{100}{100}.$$ In words, "one hundred percent" means the total $$\text{100\%}$$ is $$\frac{100}{100},$$ and since $$\frac{100}{100} = 1,$$ we see that $$\text{100\%}$$ means $$1$$ whole.

section.paragraph: Let's summarize the results from the previous examples in Table 6.1, and look for a pattern we could use to quickly convert a percent number to a decimal number.

To convert a percent number to a decimal number, we move the decimal point two places to the left and remove the $$\%$$ sign. (Sometimes the decimal point does not appear in the percent number, but just like we can think of the integer $$6$$ as $$6.0,$$ we can think of $$\text{6\%}$$ as $$\text{6.0\%} .$$ ) Notice that we may need to add zeros in front of the number when moving the decimal to the left.

section.heading: Convert Decimals and Fractions to Percents
section.paragraph: To convert a decimal to a percent, remember that percent means per hundred. If we change the decimal to a fraction whose denominator is $$100,$$ it is easy to change that fraction to a percent.

note.title: How To
note.heading: Convert a decimal to a percent.

list.item: Step 1. Write the decimal as a fraction.
Step 2. If the denominator of the fraction is not $$100,$$ rewrite it as an equivalent fraction with denominator $$100.$$
Step 3. Write this ratio as a percent.

section.paragraph: In Decimals, we learned how to convert fractions to decimals. Now we also know how to change decimals to percents. So to convert a fraction to a percent, we first change it to a decimal and then convert that decimal to a percent.

section.paragraph: Sometimes when changing a fraction to a decimal, the division continues for many decimal places and we will round off the quotient. The number of decimal places we round to will depend on the situation. If the decimal involves money, we round to the hundredths place. For most other cases in this book we will round the number to the nearest thousandth, so the percent will be rounded to the nearest tenth.

section.paragraph: When we first looked at fractions and decimals, we saw that some fractions converted to a repeating decimal. For example, when we converted the fraction $$\frac{4}{3}$$ to a decimal, we wrote the answer as $$1.\overline{3}.$$ We will use this same notation, as well as fraction notation, when we convert fractions to percents in the next example.

solution.paragraph: We could also write the percent as $$33.\overset{\_}{3}\%$$ .
